messages:
maria: heads up — customer acme-inc reported p99 regression on /v1/generate starting ~03:00Z. baseline p99 ~450ms, now seeing 2.1s-3.8s spikes. they're on a dedicated pool but via our public API. attached req ids: rq_8a1, rq_8a7, rq_8b2. can we triage?
aj: forwarded their stacktrace and an example payload (low token count, many short requests). they say it's intermittent; they hit it during small bursts. says billing unaffected.
sophie: looked at metrics for that pool. batcher wait_time_p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s at the same window. average batch size increased slightly but distribution shows more "late arrivals" — requests waiting until timeout more often. seems like continuous-batcher is aggregating a few slow-to-arrive micro-requests into existing batches.
maria: hmm. any config drift recently? or rollout?
ethan: no recent infra rollout. there was a runtime tweak last week that enabled sticky-routing for session affinity (to reduce KV cache churn). suspect interaction: sticky routing + bursty tiny requests -> some shards get many small inflight requests that miss early batching and force longer timeouts.
sophie: here's current batcher config we deploy to that pool:
```
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 120
  prefer_local_shard: true
  max_waiting_requests_per_shard: 256
```
notice batch_timeout is 120ms which normally balances throughput/latency. but when you get many almost-simultaneous tiny requests that arrive slightly after the batch is dispatched, they wait full timeout -> tail blowup.
aj: customer provided a replay script. attaching simplified repro: they do 200 concurrent clients each sending 1-3 token prompts with 10-30ms jitter.
ethan: to reproduce quickly on staging:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  (for j in {1..50}; do 
    sleep $(awk -v min=0.01 -v max=0.03 'BEGIN{srand(); print min+rand()*(max-min)}')
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Priority: normal" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null &
  done; wait) &
done; wait
```
this reproduces p99 wait spikes on the batcher in staging.
maria: ok immediate mitigations we can try (ranked):
1) temporary: reduce batch_timeout_ms from 120 -> 40 for that pool (reduces tail but increases compute per-token)
2) enable small-request fastlane: if Content-Length < N or header X-Client-Priority=high route to non-batched low-latency workers
3) lower max_waiting_requests_per_shard to reduce queuing (avoid head-of-line blocking)
4) revert/adjust sticky-routing heuristics so requests distribute more evenly across shards
which one can we do quickly?
sophie: (1) is trivial config change and rollout via configmap -> rolling restart. (2) needs routing rule + infra work, not immediate. (3) is quick but might drop capacity. (4) needs careful canary.
ethan: I'd do (1) + (3) as hotfix. patching now to a canary subset of nodes so we can watch p95/p99.
ops-bot: starting canary rollout for config batch_timeout_ms=40 on pool pool-acme-1 — patch id patch-2026-03-15-01
maria: monitor plan: watch batcher.wait_time_p99, batch_size_distribution, inference_cpu_util, and customer p99. set alert threshold for >1s.
aj: pinged acme support with repro steps and told them we're investigating and will apply a hotfix. they asked if there's a workaround on their side — suggested adding 5-10ms client-side jitter (staggering) as temporary measure.
sophie: applied canary to 3 nodes. early signals: batcher.wait_time_p99 dropped ~65% on canary; avg batch size down ~10%. cpu per-token cost up ~8% (expected).
maria: nice. ops-bot, roll out to remaining nodes with 5m pause and auto-rollback on error?
ops-bot: rolling out patch-2026-03-15-01 to remaining nodes in pool-acme-1 with pause=300s; rollback_on_alerts=[batcher.wait_time_p99>1s, error_rate>0.5%]
ethan: while that rolls, I'll draft a follow-up: implement prioritization header and add routing rule. also we should add an adaptive timeout that reduces batch_timeout for shards with high late_arrival_ratio.
maria: agreed. create GH issue for adaptive-timeout + fastlane. link it here when created.
aj: customer updated: after our hotfix they're seeing p99 drop back to acceptable levels. will keep them in loop. :thumbsup:
sophie: created GH issue #4321 "adaptive continuous batch timeout + fastlane for small requests" and added initial design notes.
maria: next steps captured:
- hotfix rolled and verified (completed)
- create adaptive timeout + fastlane design (GH #4321)
- monitor similar pools for same pattern (write query)
- add replay test in CI that mimics bursty micro-requests (ethan to own)
aj: closing loop with customer now. thanks team.
ethan: filed replay test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-replays/pull/212
maria: great work all. noted: this is a good reminder that continuous batching heuristics need special casing for high-frequency tiny requests. :eyes:
